finding.claim: wipe() ignores the boolean returned by requireRole(), so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. They control the `tenant` path parameter and hold no OWNER role.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive operation on tenant data.

trace.note: requireRole returns a boolean and does not throw (see the javadoc at line 13).
The return value is discarded as a bare statement, so a non-owner passes through.
repo.wipe(tenant) runs unconditionally with the attacker-supplied tenant.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is requireRole at line 26, and its result is unused. No other authorization, tenant-membership or ownership check exists on this path. The sibling export() at line 32 correctly uses checkRole, which throws, so it is not affected by this bug.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole at src/Admin.java:26 returns a boolean and does not throw (lines 13-16). Its result is discarded. No other check exists on this path.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") as a bare statement, so its boolean result (defined at line 14-16, non-throwing) is discarded and repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() at line 32, which uses the throwing checkRole.
